targets.exactResearchQuestion: Does methodology 1.0 require quantified accelerator end-customer concentration and switching/share economics before AMD can be promoted, or can customer concentration, moat and pricing be scored reproducibly from current primary evidence with explicit unknowns?
targets.gateAtStart: GATING: issuer evidence still does not quantify accelerator end-customer concentration or switching/share economics sufficiently for reproducible moat/pricing treatment.
targets.summary: The exact subsegment concentration/share precision requested by the blocked-queue note is not itself a locked methodology field. Methodology requires customer diversification/concentration, moat/differentiation, pricing power and confidence to be scored with sourced evidence. AMD's 2025 10-K explicitly flags significant-customer loss risk but does not provide a quantified >=10% major-customer table; its current primary evidence nevertheless demonstrates multiple independent production/deployment relationships across Meta, OpenAI, Microsoft, xAI and Oracle. Q1 2026 Data Center revenue was $5.775B with $1.599B segment operating income, and total-company gross margin was 53%, giving reproducible operating evidence. Therefore Chief can score concentration/diversification and moat/pricing conservatively with lower confidence instead of holding promotion for unavailable exact accelerator revenue-share data.

evidence.fact: AMD Q1 2026 Data Center revenue was $5.775B and Data Center operating income was $1.599B; consolidated gross margin was 53%.
AMD's 2025 Form 10-K explicitly identifies loss of a significant customer as a material business risk, so customer concentration must remain visible even without a quantified accelerator-only split.
AMD states seven of the ten largest model builders/AI companies were running production workloads on Instinct, naming Meta, OpenAI, Microsoft and xAI; Oracle was also deploying MI355X infrastructure.
AMD and Meta announced a multi-year, multi-generation agreement for up to 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPU deployments, with first-gigawatt shipments expected in 2H 2026.
Oracle announced a public AI supercluster with an initial 50,000 AMD MI450 GPUs planned from Q3 2026, providing an independent named hyperscaler deployment path beyond Meta.

inference: Multiple named production/deployment relationships are sufficient to avoid treating accelerator demand as a single-customer proposition, but they do not prove equal revenue distribution.
Exact accelerator end-customer revenue concentration and durable market-share persistence are useful confidence enhancers, not explicit mandatory fields in methodology.ts/rubric.ts.
Pricing-power treatment should be conservative because issuer price/performance benchmarks do not substitute for independently observed realized pricing.
contradictions: A broad named customer set coexists with a very large Meta forward commitment; diversification evidence does not eliminate concentration risk.
Strong Data Center growth and margins demonstrate current economics but do not prove durable accelerator switching costs or future share.

unknowns.item: Exact Instinct/accelerator revenue concentration by hyperscaler/end customer
Durable accelerator market share and realized switching economics versus NVIDIA/custom silicon

falsifiers: A later filing discloses a dominant accelerator customer concentration materially greater than currently implied by the named deployment breadth.
Production deployments fail to translate into durable Data Center segment margins or repeat orders across multiple customers.
ROCm/platform switching friction remains insufficient and major customers migrate materially toward competing accelerators/custom silicon.
targets.nextBestSourcePath: If Chief wants higher confidence rather than gate closure, use future 10-Q/10-K major-customer disclosure and customer procurement/deployment disclosures; do not hold promotion solely for an accelerator-only concentration percentage that the issuer does not publish.

targets.exactResearchQuestion: Can current primary evidence quantify TSMC customer concentration and overseas-fab/capex economics sufficiently for reproducible customer-concentration, balance-sheet/capital-efficiency, geographic-diversification and risk treatment?
targets.gateAtStart: GATING: disclosed major-customer dependence and overseas-fab/capex economics still require reproducible concentration/capital-efficiency treatment.
targets.summary: Primary 2025 Form 20-F and 2026 earnings disclosures resolve the requested concentration and overseas-fab economics bridge. TSMC's top ten customers were 78% of 2025 revenue; the largest customer was 19% and the second largest 17%. 2025 capex was about US$40.9B and 2026 capex guidance is US$52B-US$56B, funded primarily through operating cash flow and corporate bonds. Arizona Fab 21 entered high-volume production at end-2024; the U.S. CHIPS agreement provides up to $6.6B direct funding and up to $5B government loans subject to conditions. Management explicitly quantifies overseas-fab gross-margin dilution at 2%-3% in early years, widening to 3%-4% later, while Q2 2026 consolidated gross margin was 67.7%. These are sufficient inputs for reproducible concentration/capital-efficiency risk treatment.

evidence.fact: TSMC's ten largest customers represented 78% of 2025 net revenue; largest customer 19%, second largest 17%.
TSMC 2025 capex was NT$1.272T (about US$40.895B); 2026 capex is expected at US$52B-US$56B and funded by operating cash flow and corporate bonds.
Arizona Fab 21 first facility entered high-volume production at end-2024; CHIPS Act direct funding is up to US$6.6B plus up to US$5B in government loans, subject to milestone/compliance conditions.

TSMC Q2 2026 gross margin was 67.7%; management continues to forecast overseas-fab gross-margin dilution of 2%-3% in early stages and 3%-4% in later stages while noting very strong leading-edge demand and ongoing utilization/cost optimization.
TSMC Q2 2026 actual gross margin was 67.7% and operating margin 60.3%.

inference: Customer concentration is high and explicitly measurable, so the customer-concentration risk factor can be scored without guessing identities.
Overseas expansion is a real margin drag, but its magnitude is explicitly bounded by management and currently coexists with very high consolidated margins and internally funded capex capacity.
Specific Arizona fab utilization is not disclosed, but methodology does not require fab-level utilization when consolidated utilization/margin dilution/capex funding evidence is available.
contradictions: TSMC describes its 534-customer base as diversified, yet revenue economics are concentrated: top ten customers are 78% of revenue.
Geographic manufacturing diversification reduces single-region exposure but creates structurally higher overseas costs and margin dilution.

unknowns.item: Exact Fab 21 standalone utilization and unit economics

falsifiers: Overseas-fab dilution persistently exceeds management's 3%-4% later-stage range without compensating utilization/productivity gains.
Largest-customer concentration rises materially while switching/substitution risk increases.
Capex growth materially outpaces operating cash generation and requires balance-sheet stress inconsistent with current self-funding evidence.
targets.nextBestSourcePath: For later confidence refinement, monitor 2026 Form 20-F/customer concentration and quarterly commentary on overseas-fab dilution; fab-specific utilization should remain unknown unless the issuer publishes it.

targets.exactResearchQuestion: Can current primary evidence quantify ASML China/export exposure and critical-supplier dependence sufficiently for reproducible regulatory, geographic-diversification and supply-chain-resilience risk treatment?
targets.gateAtStart: GATING: current China/export exposure and disclosed critical-supplier dependence are not yet encoded as a reproducible factor/risk record.
targets.summary: Current primary evidence resolves the requested risk record. China represented 29.1% of ASML's 2025 total net sales, while Q2 2026 China represented 14% of quarterly net system sales by ship-to location (down from 19% in Q1 2026), consistent with prior guidance that 2026 China sales would decline from unusually strong 2024-2025 levels. ASML's 2025 annual report identifies Carl Zeiss SMT as the sole supplier of critical lithography optics under an exclusive arrangement and states that prolonged loss of Zeiss optics supply could effectively stop ASML's business. The report also identifies 272 business-critical suppliers accounting for 89% of product-related spend. These disclosures provide a reproducible basis for strong supplier-concentration and export/regulatory risk penalties without waiting for unknowable future export rules.

evidence.fact: China customers represented 29.1% of ASML 2025 total net sales (36.1% in 2024).
Q2 2026 net system sales by ship-to region were 14% China versus 19% in Q1 2026; Taiwan 30%, South Korea 43%, USA 9%, Japan 4% in Q2.

ASML's 2025 annual report identifies Carl Zeiss SMT as its sole supplier of lenses, mirrors, illuminators, collectors and other critical optics under an exclusive arrangement; prolonged inability to supply optics could effectively prevent ASML from conducting its business.
ASML had 272 business-critical suppliers generating 89% of product-related spend in 2025; business-critical includes unique/single-source items, >12-week switching time or long production times.
ASML Q2 2026 total net sales were EUR9.3B, gross margin 54.0%, and full-year 2026 guidance was raised to EUR43B-EUR45B despite ongoing export-control risk.

inference: ASML's China exposure is large but measurable and already declining in current quarterly system-sales mix, allowing a current regulatory/geographic risk score without forecasting future rules.
Zeiss dependence is an unusually strong single-supplier risk and should materially penalize supplyChainResilience even though ASML's broader supplier base is geographically diversified.
The combination of 2026 growth/margin guidance and explicit supplier/export disclosures supports scoring present resilience/risk without treating future policy outcomes as known.
contradictions: ASML's extraordinary bottleneck control over advanced lithography coexists with its own severe upstream bottleneck dependence on Zeiss optics.
China exposure is falling from 2024-2025 highs, but export-policy sensitivity remains material because policy can affect both system sales and serviceability.

unknowns.item: Future U.S./Dutch/multilateral export-control scope and license outcomes
Exact recovery time if Zeiss suffers a prolonged production outage

falsifiers: China exposure unexpectedly re-accelerates while policy restrictions tighten enough to strand material backlog/service economics.
Zeiss capacity fails to scale with ASML's planned 2027-2028 EUV/DUV capacity expansion.
Supplier concentration causes sustained shipment shortfalls or margin degradation inconsistent with current backlog/guidance.
targets.nextBestSourcePath: For later updates, use ASML quarterly regional system-sales presentations and annual-report supplier-risk disclosures. Do not block promotion on future export restrictions that have not occurred.
